summary.headline: JSW Energy added 873 MW in Q1 FY27 (about 1.1 GW since April) and holds ₹12,880 crore cash, while net debt is about ₹55,000 crore and TTM net leverage is 4.95x.
summary.overview: Revenue was flat YoY at ₹5,437 crore and EBITDA rose 2% to ₹3,103 crore, while PAT fell to ₹533 crore (₹471 crore attributable) on higher depreciation (+20% to ₹890 crore) and interest (+16% to ₹1,519 crore) from new capacity. Net generation fell 5% YoY to 12.9 BU, with hydro down about 26% on weak hydrology and thermal down 6%, partly offset by solar up 29%. Management reiterated FY27 targets of 3 GW capacity addition and ₹20,000 crore capex, and outlined a pumped storage pipeline, the Maruti Clean Coal acquisition, and a 600 MW Mahanadi unit 4 for FY28.

segments.name: Renewables (solar and wind)
segments.commentary: Solar generation rose 29% and wind 3% YoY, supported by 1,168 MW of added capacity; renewables are about 61% of the 14.6 GW installed base. Solar PLF was about 21-22% in Q1 and management expects a higher second half.

segments.name: Hydro
segments.commentary: Portfolio generation fell about 26% YoY on weak hydrology (Sutlej basin -39%, Ravi -24%, national -7%) despite Tidong and Kutehr additions. Karcham, Baspa and Kutehr were above 100% PLF in July.

segments.name: Thermal
segments.commentary: Thermal generation fell 6% YoY to 8 BU; Mahanadi lost about 184 MU (about 7%) due to a 17-day evacuation outage, which management says falls under force majeure. Thermal fleet is 5.7 GW, with open capacity under 4%.

segments.name: Battery storage (BESS) assembly
segments.commentary: The 5 GWh battery plant won a first large external order of about ₹440 crore; management guides to about $2.75-3/kWh margin, roughly $15 million a year and close to ₹150 crore EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target of 3 GW capacity addition and ₹20,000 crore capex reaffirmed; about 1.1 GW already added since April, with about 225 MW more in July.
Net leverage to be below 5x by 2030; FY28 capacity addition guided to be in the same range (about 3 GW), with FY28 connectivity details promised soon.
Mahanadi unit 4 (600 MW) targeted for commissioning in FY28, taking the plant from 1.8 GW to 3.6 GW; capex expected to be 25-30% lower than greenfield.

Preferential promoter allotment balance of about ₹1,875 crore due before June 2027; management expects operating cash flow plus fundraise proceeds to cover about ₹12,000-12,500 crore of the ₹20,000 crore capex.
Bhavali (1,500 MW) and Kandhaura (1,680 MW; 1,500 MW PPA signed with UP) pumped storage projects; management expects significantly high-teen IRRs. Narihalla (Karnataka) PPA expected soon.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 commissioning of 873 MW, including 150 MW early commissioning of Tidong Hydro (originally October 2026) that added ₹20-22 crore EBITDA in Q1.

Connectivity: 300 MW under TGNA expected to convert to GNA before 31 August; 400 MW O2 Power (Rajasthan) connectivity now expected September-October. Management says the remaining 1.9 GW of FY27 additions is fully connected, with about 530 MW off-grid captive.

Salboni 2x800 MW: TG order placed with Toshiba JSW Power Systems, land fully acquired, site work underway. GE Durgapur boiler facility acquisition expected by end of Q1; nameplate 1.1 GW, targeted 1.6 GW after debottlenecking.
Halol (Gujarat) wind blade plant commissioned 8 June 2026 with 450 blades per year (about 600 MW of wind); Chitradurga plant expected by FY27.

Pumped storage readiness: Bhavali has environment clearance, land mostly acquired, L&T civil and Voith electromechanical orders placed; Kandhaura awaiting forest clearance and connectivity, with readiness expected in Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 national power demand grew 8.5% YoY (July month-to-date about 12%); peak demand hit 271 GW in May, above FY26's 245 GW peak.
DAM prices averaged ₹5.10/unit in Q1 FY27 vs about ₹4.40 in Q1 FY26 (about 16% higher).
API4 coal index rose to $113 in Q1 FY27 from $90 in Q1 FY26 (about 25%); management says it is resilient through its shift to domestic coal.
Management said it is seeing buyer interest for 600 MW-scale thermal PPAs, citing imported-coal replacement demand.
Maruti Clean Coal & Power (300 MW Chhattisgarh): 195 MW net PPA with Rajasthan discoms (14-year residual life), about 64 MW merchant; acquisition agreement signed.

qa_highlights.question: How is the thermal fleet handling sub-technical-minimum operation during midday solar hours?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Mahanadi backdowns were minimal under merit order, Utkal minimum load stayed at or above 60%, and July PLF was above 85% with availability above 90%. Fixed costs are recovered during backdowns.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of boiler sourcing for Mahanadi unit 4 and Salboni?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahanadi unit 4 is about 30-40% complete with BoP ready; equipment is Chinese-sourced and under dispatch. Salboni TG is with TJPS; the GE Durgapur boiler facility (1.1 GW nameplate) is expected to be acquired by end-Q1 and debottlenecked to 1.6 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin on the BESS external order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to about $2.75-3/kWh, roughly $15 million a year, or close to ₹150 crore EBITDA. It sees backward integration into cells as the next value-add step, with no long-term cell supplier yet.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 1.9 GW of remaining FY27 projects connected, and what about FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all 1.9 GW is connected, including 530 MW off-grid captive. FY28 connectivity details will come later.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the lower thermal PLFs, especially at Utkal and Ratnagiri?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Utkal's drop to a planned unit shutdown for annual availability in Q1, with availability above 91% in July. Ratnagiri's drop was a planned shutdown plus weaker June demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT under pressure and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said interest is higher during early years post-commissioning, and EBITDA-to-PBT conversion should improve as assets stabilise over 4-5 years.

risks_watch: Weak hydrology: Q1 hydro generation down about 26% YoY; monsoon recovery in July is the key check.
Curtailment: 69 MU of wind and solar curtailed in Q1 (about ₹15 crore revenue impact); 300 MW TGNA conversion by 31 August and 400 MW Rajasthan connectivity in September-October.
Project execution: pumped storage timelines, Mahanadi unit 4 (FY28), the GE boiler acquisition, and the Chitradurga blade plant by FY27.
Balance sheet: about ₹1,875 crore of promoter preferential money due before June 2027; gross debt about ₹74,000 crore, and FY28 funding needs still to be disclosed.
Mahanadi evacuation outage (17 days, about 184 MU) to be recognised under force majeure; the outcome is not yet confirmed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and detailed, especially on capacity additions, connectivity and pumped storage returns. Management was more guarded on FY28 targets (deferred to a later update) and on PAT trajectory, which it attributed to depreciation and interest timing.
